Jian W.: Hi team — my medical exam required for the visa got bumped; earliest slot is May 20. My start is May 3 and I planned to fly in May 1. Does this block me from onboarding in-person?
Maria HR: thanks for the heads up Jian. If medical is pending and you can still enter the country with your current stamp, payroll/onboarding can proceed. If the visa stamping itself depends on the medical, we need immigration to confirm.
Alyssa (Immigration): @Jian quick clarification: for some visa categories the panel physician report is required before stamping. If your consulate requires the medical before visa issuance, you'll be delayed. If you already have a valid visa, you can enter and finish medical domestically in some cases. Send your consulate instructions and we can advise.
Jian W.: consulate email says "medical required prior to appointment". Looks like stamping will be after May 20. What are options if I can't get into the country by May 3?
Elena (Relocation): on relocation side — if travel delays push your arrival past the relocation payout milestone (arrival within 30 days of start), we can do a delayed disbursement. We need proof of appointment and any changed flight receipts. The lump-sum sign-off is by payroll so we'll coordinate.
Maria HR: policy-wise we offer two common paths: 1) deferred official start date until after you arrive/stamp, or 2) remote start from abroad for up to 14 days with manager approval. For benefits, effective date follows the official payroll start. If you're paid on May 3 but not physically present, health insurance can start but dependents may require verification later.
people-ops-bot: Please attach consulate correspondence and panel physician confirmation to https://redwood/hr/cases/jian-medical (case created: HR-2026-5710).
Jian W.: manager approved remote start for two weeks. If I remote from outside country, will relocation still cover temporary housing?
Elena (Relocation): temporary housing is tied to physical relocation. If you delay arrival, we'll prorate hotel nights. We can hold the credit for 90 days while you complete stamping. Upload appointment docs and we'll add a note.
Alyssa (Immigration): FYI also check vaccination records for the panel doctor; sometimes you need additional shots and that adds to timeline. If the visa is delayed >60 days, we escalate to enterprise immigration lawyer for options.
Maria HR: Jian — also confirm whether tax residency changes if you start while abroad. Payroll may need to set withholding differently if you are paid but non-resident that pay period. Rebecca from payroll can advise once you confirm remote-work country.
Jian W.: noted. Last Q: will the relocation lump sum be taxed differently if paid after I start?
Elena (Relocation): relocation payments are handled as a one-time taxable benefit. Timing doesn't change tax treatment but country of payment can affect withholding. We'll coordinate with payroll for a clear breakdown before payment.
Jian W.: great, I'll upload the consulate email and the appointment confirmation by EOD. Thanks everyone.
Maria HR: keeping this thread as the case trail. Tag me when you upload and we'll finalize the start date and benefits window.
people-ops-bot: Ticket updated: HR-2026-5710 — documents added pending (consulate email, appointment).
